entities.name: Kanishka III
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Kanishka III, the Kushan Samrat, ruled from 265 CE to 270 CE in the vast expanse of Northwestern India, bridging the ancient world of the Silk Road to the Indian subcontinent. 

 Born into a dynasty that had previously ruled the Indian subcontinent, Kanishka III's ascension to the throne marked a pivotal moment in the region's history, as he navigated the complex web of alliances and rivalries between various Indo-Greek kingdoms and the emerging power of the Gupta Empire. 

 His reign was marked by a series of key events, including the Edicts of Kanishka, a set of inscriptions that promoted Buddhism, tolerance, and the rule of law, which were carved into rock faces across the ancient world. 

 Kanishka III's legacy extends far beyond his own time, as his policies and decisions had a lasting impact on the development of the Indian subcontinent, influencing the trajectory of Buddhist history and the rise of the Gupta Empire, which would go on to shape the course of Indian history for centuries to come. 

 As a testament to his enduring legacy, Kanishka III remains an important figure in the annals of Indian history, his name invoked alongside those of other great rulers who have shaped the destinies of empires and civilizations.
